A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIP study. Their main text, equations, Tables 1–10, Figures 1–7, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation and depth-prediction experiments, ablations, and additional quantitative and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the work's original benchmark results, ablations, and appendix analyses. Retained results still constitute original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same pseudo-task construction, DiffCut/DINOv2R pseudo-labeling, positive and distractor sampling, cross-attention predictions, cross-entropy objective, and downstream retrieval procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use COCO and ImageNet for post-training and retain the same segmentation datasets, Cityscapes-to-ACDC scenario, NYUv2 depth task, and appendix linear-segmentation evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the reported experiments, including DINOv2R/NeCo comparisons and the SD, SAM, and RADIOv2.5 comparison in Table 5. The newly cited Franca work is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Table 5 changes the reported DINOv2R and DIP backbones from ViT-B/16 to ViT-B/14, resolving an inconsistency with Section 4.1 and other tables. This is a reported configuration correction; unchanged scores do not establish that experiments were rerun. Other settings are retained.

E4.justification: The objective, distractor, positive-example, DiffCut, pseudo-class-count, training-dataset, temperature, and memory-size analyses are retained. Appendix ablations and qualitative examples also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical scores in Tables 1–10, plotted curves, and qualitative examples are retained. For example, Table 1 still reports DIP ViT-B/14 scores of 82.1 and 42.6 with full PascalVOC and ADE20K data. Table 5 changes backbone labels without changing performance values.

T1.justification: The task and feature definitions, attention equations, label aggregation, and expected cross-entropy objective in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about unsupervised, meta-learning-inspired post-training, computational efficiency, improved dense representations, and generalization across segmentation and depth tasks.

C2.justification: The introduction expands the rationale for calling DIP unsupervised. Whereas v1 emphasizes the absence of dense segmentation annotations, v2 additionally explains that captions are not used when extracting segments from Stable Diffusion.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies caption-free Stable Diffusion segment extraction and corrects the backbone identifiers in Table 5. Appendix A's implementation details, hyperparameters, training times, hardware information, and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Franca [75] to the introduction and self-supervised-learning discussion, and cites the already-listed BYOL work for the EMA-teacher explanation. Other bibliography edits update existing works without substantially changing research positioning.

P1.justification: Substantial prose rewriting and compression span the abstract, introduction, Related Work subsections, method exposition, and experimental discussion. Headings are standardized and a supplementary-material title is added, while the overall section sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: Existing displays are repositioned: Figure 4 moves from page 6 to page 5, and Tables 5–6 and Figure 5 are reflowed. v2 adds page numbers and a supplementary title. Graphics, axes, legends, and table structures otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The Table 5 backbone correction resolves an internal reporting inconsistency, and the caption-free extraction clarification makes the supervision used easier to understand. Condensed exposition and clearer supplementary labeling improve readability while preserving the original experimental and appendix evidence. The overall gains are limited to clarity and reporting accuracy.
